risks.risk: Raw material and commodity cost inflation
risks.note: The conflict in the middle east has raised commodity prices, with a risk premium likely to get added particularly to Crude; commodity prices are at an elevated level now which management says will impact margins in financial year 2026-27, and prices are expected to remain elevated for some time even after the conflict ends.

risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict and supply-chain / freight disruption
risks.note: Management states the world economy continues to be affected by geo political tensions and tariff related uncertainties, which will result in global slow down and impact demand in both domestic and export markets; the conflict has raised shipping costs and supply chain vulnerabilities, and the conflict in Iran caused substantial disruptions to the supply chain and to exports to the middle east, traditionally a very strong geography for the Company.

The Rupee depreciated 10% over the last year and 4% since the conflict began; rupee depreciation along with higher commodity costs can result in higher inflation, translate into higher interest rates and lower Government spending, and impact the economy negatively.

risks.risk: Below-normal monsoon and weak rural demand
risks.note: The forecast of a below normal monsoon is flagged as a negative that will impact the agricultural sector, rural demand and consumption — directly relevant given the tractor/farm tyre exposure — and all these could result in margin pressures for the tyre industry.

Uncertainty around United States tariffs continues, with global trade patterns shifting and geo economic fragmentation and geo political risks increasingly becoming a reality; global automakers, including European ones, face regulatory change, trade tension and uncertain economic outlook, which conditions demand for tyres.

Export momentum in the second half was constrained by economic challenges in the Philippines, political developments in Bangladesh and election cycles in select African nations, alongside the Middle East disruption — showing the export book's sensitivity to a handful of geographies.

Industrial relations were cordial except for a few instances of work disruption in the Arkonam, Tiruvottiyur and Trichy plants; long term settlements in the Trichy plants have not been completed and are under negotiation.

risks.risk: Regulatory and technology transition in tyres
risks.note: The tyre industry is undergoing rapid transformation driven by sustainability goals, electric mobility, digitalization and performance demands, requiring continuous technology absorption; regulatory compliance under R117 and AIS 142 standards obliges development of low rolling resistance and low-noise tyres without compromising safety and durability.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: MRF is India's leading tyre manufacturer, supplying tyres across commercial vehicle, passenger vehicle, two-wheeler and farm segments to Original Equipment manufacturers and the replacement market in India and to export markets.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: MRF manufactures and sells tyres for commercial vehicles, passenger vehicles, two-wheelers and tractors/farm equipment, selling both as an Original Equipment (OE) fitment to India's vehicle manufacturers and into the replacement market. The Company is a preferred OE fitment supplier to most of India's large OEMs, is fitted on most of India's top-selling passenger vehicles including next-generation EV models, and describes itself as the most preferred supplier of tyres to Electric Vehicles. It also exports tyres — including truck and light-truck radial, 3-wheeler and farm tyre categories — to markets across Africa, the Middle East, South East Asia, Europe and the Americas.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Strong traction in automobile sales is likely to continue in the current year, which management says would be beneficial to tyre companies
- GST 2.0 rate cuts announced on 22 September 2025 revived demand across vehicle categories, and demand buoyancy continued through the second half of the year
- The Company expects to continue its growth based on its strong brand presence and product portfolio despite margin pressure
- Margins are likely to be impacted by higher commodity prices and transport costs; commodity prices are at an elevated level after a year of easing costs
- A below normal monsoon with El Nino conditions can moderate tractor sales and dampen rural demand, a negative for tyre companies, and makes the FY27 tractor outlook moderate against a high FY26 base
- Tractor demand support from the GST reduction effect and the ongoing shift towards farm mechanisation and high yielding crops, plus deep OEM ties
- M&HCV truck industry grew close to 15% in FY2025-26 as GST revision let large fleet operators replace old fleets; the year ahead could see a surge in truck production in the first quarter and a relatively flat performance thereafter
- Second phase of AIS 142 norms likely in the second half of FY2026-27 will impact OEM use of nylon tyres, as nylon tyres will not meet noise levels
- Passenger vehicle industry grew 9% in FY2025-26; MRF outperformed the industry and improved market share in the PV OE segment, with replacement demand aided by new launches and rising SUV tyre sales
- Two-wheeler industry in its third consecutive year of expansion, with electric two-wheeler monthly sales stabilising near the 1 lakh unit milestone signalling a permanent shift in urban mobility
- Tyre industry grew an estimated 10% in 2025-26 and Indian tyre exports grew 9%
- Export recovery depends on global supply chain and economic conditions stabilising; the Middle East conflict disrupted supply chains and exports to a traditionally strong geography, while Sri Lanka, Brazil and select African and Middle East markets grew well
- Domestic demand continues to be strong as evidenced by passenger car sales of April 2026, and trade agreements concluded in FY2025-26 should start yielding benefits
- Risks to demand from possible fuel price increases lowering disposable income, higher fiscal deficit curtailing government expenditure, further rupee depreciation and imported inflation forcing RBI rate increases

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Consolidate market share in both the replacement and Original Equipment (OE) segments across commercial vehicle, passenger vehicle, two-wheeler and farm categories
- Strengthen the OE franchise — remain the preferred fitment supplier to India's large OEMs, including on next-generation EV models and on premium two-wheelers exported to regulated markets such as Europe, Brazil and the US
- Move up the technology curve: first-in-India 20-inch rim size OE tyres for domestic PVs and acoustic foam tyres for EVs for in-cabin noise reduction
- Expand into the high-performance superbike segment with specialised high-speed rated radials, transitioning from a high-volume manufacturer to a technical partner competing globally
- Keep innovation central — develop advanced tyre solutions for all vehicle segments from two-wheelers to heavy commercial vehicles and construction equipment, while expanding the range of eco-friendly and sustainable products
- Grow the global footprint through targeted expansions in Africa, South East Asia and Europe, supported by new truck radial and farm radial launches aimed at Europe and the Americas
- Protect profitability through operational management and cost-control initiatives in the face of higher petro-based raw material prices and shipping freight rates
- Systematically reduce the carbon footprint and drive towards carbon neutrality in support of India's National Net Zero vision
- Increase the share of renewable electricity in operations
- Improve energy efficiency through natural ventilation systems, nitrogen gas-based processes, energy-efficient compressors and biomass blending with existing boiler fuels
- Optimise water use efficiency for long-term water security, including installation of additional wastewater recovery plants
- Expand the MRF Corp (Paints Division) retail portfolio with new innovations and targeted line extensions
- Pursue the CSR vision of inclusive and sustainable development through education, healthcare, skill development, safe drinking water, rural development, environmental sustainability, women empowerment and sports promotion
- Dividends are declared in accordance with the Company's dividend distribution policy: the Board declared interim dividends during the year and has recommended a final dividend on equity shares for consideration and approval of shareholders at the forthcoming Annual General Meeting, with the balance of profits after taxation and dividend transferred to general reserve. The Company has kept its balance sheet conservative — it discontinued acceptance of fixed deposits with effect from 31st March, 2019 and has repaid all deposits with no fresh deposits accepted since, and during the year under review it gave no loan, security or guarantee in terms of section 186 of the Companies Act, 2013. No shares with differential voting rights and no sweat equity shares have been issued. The Board periodically reviews capital expenditure proposals along with operations and statutory compliance.
- Continuous improvement programme to reduce specific consumption of fuel, power, water and carbon footprint, with targets set from benchmarking best performance and base-lining best consumption, tracked through an Energy Monitoring system
- Adoption of the ISO 50001 energy management standard to create awareness and ensure continual improvement and energy-consumption reduction
- Increased sourcing of renewable energy and increased usage of biomass towards sustainability and carbon neutrality
- Biomass blending in the existing coal-based steam generation system to reduce carbon footprint, with evaluation of biomass-based boilers in place of conventional fuels as an ongoing proposal
- Trials initiated with pyrolysis oil and char in boilers, and conversion of boiler burners to dual fuel to utilise cleaner energy fuels
- Horizontal deployment of waste water treatment plants to reuse treated water in process, plus recycling of municipal waste water and ETP/waste-water recovery plant output back into the process
- Initiative on ISO 46001 systems to create awareness on water conservation and to ensure a system for water-consumption reduction
- Phase-out of diesel-based material handling equipment in favour of electric operated equipment
- Energy-efficiency measures including natural ventilation replacing forced ventilation, LED lighting replacing induction lamps, energy-efficient compressors and AHUs in HVAC, waste heat recovery in boilers and nitrogen-based curing processes
- Improved share of circular materials in all tyres, and R&D in sustainable and circular raw materials, bio-based and recycled materials
- Development of low rolling resistance tyres for regulatory compliance under R117 and AIS 142 without compromising safety and durability, and tyres with low pass-by noise and better in-cabin acoustic comfort
- BRSR for the financial year ended 31st March 2026 published in the prescribed format with reasonable assurance on BRSR Core indicators from SGS India Pvt. Ltd., Mumbai
- Board-level Risk Management Committee whose remit expressly includes sustainability related matters and business continuity planning

moat.body:
- Leading position in the Indian tyre industry with a strong brand presence that management credits for continued growth
- Preferred OE fitment supplier to most of India's large OEMs and a fitment on most of India's top-selling passenger vehicles, including next-generation EV models
- Most preferred supplier of tyres to Electric Vehicles besides being one of the largest OE suppliers of tyres to ICE vehicles
- Market leadership in the two-wheeler segment, being the preferred fitment choice across nearly all new OEM launches and segments
- Unrivalled dominance in the replacement market driven by consumer preference for proven performance and durability
- Technology leadership — first in India to supply 20-inch rim size tyres in the OE segment for domestic PVs and introduction of acoustic foam tyres for EVs
- Deep OEM ties and market presence in tractors, enabling record sales growth and increased share of business with tractor manufacturers
- Broad product portfolio spanning commercial vehicles, passenger vehicles, two-wheelers and farm, with new SKU launches aiding performance
- Integrated ERP system connecting all plants, sales offices and head office, supporting internal control across a growing operation

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Raw material and commodity cost inflation — The conflict in the middle east has raised commodity prices, with a risk premium likely to get added particularly to Crude; commodity prices are at an elevated level now which management says will impact margins in financial year 2026-27, and prices are expected to remain elevated for some time even after the conflict ends.
- Geopolitical conflict and supply-chain / freight disruption — Management states the world economy continues to be affected by geo political tensions and tariff related uncertainties, which will result in global slow down and impact demand in both domestic and export markets; the conflict has raised shipping costs and supply chain vulnerabilities, and the conflict in Iran caused substantial disruptions to the supply chain and to exports to the middle east, traditionally a very strong geography for the Company.
- Rupee depreciation and imported inflation — The Rupee depreciated 10% over the last year and 4% since the conflict began; rupee depreciation along with higher commodity costs can result in higher inflation, translate into higher interest rates and lower Government spending, and impact the economy negatively.
- Below-normal monsoon and weak rural demand — The forecast of a below normal monsoon is flagged as a negative that will impact the agricultural sector, rural demand and consumption — directly relevant given the tractor/farm tyre exposure — and all these could result in margin pressures for the tyre industry.
- Tariff and trade-policy uncertainty — Uncertainty around United States tariffs continues, with global trade patterns shifting and geo economic fragmentation and geo political risks increasingly becoming a reality; global automakers, including European ones, face regulatory change, trade tension and uncertain economic outlook, which conditions demand for tyres.
- Export-market concentration and country-specific disruption — Export momentum in the second half was constrained by economic challenges in the Philippines, political developments in Bangladesh and election cycles in select African nations, alongside the Middle East disruption — showing the export book's sensitivity to a handful of geographies.
- Industrial relations at manufacturing units — Industrial relations were cordial except for a few instances of work disruption in the Arkonam, Tiruvottiyur and Trichy plants; long term settlements in the Trichy plants have not been completed and are under negotiation.
- Regulatory and technology transition in tyres — The tyre industry is undergoing rapid transformation driven by sustainability goals, electric mobility, digitalization and performance demands, requiring continuous technology absorption; regulatory compliance under R117 and AIS 142 standards obliges development of low rolling resistance and low-noise tyres without compromising safety and durability.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Consolidate market share in both the replacement and Original Equipment (OE) segments across commercial vehicle, passenger vehicle, two-wheeler and farm categories
- Strengthen the OE franchise — remain the preferred fitment supplier to India's large OEMs, including on next-generation EV models and on premium two-wheelers exported to regulated markets such as Europe, Brazil and the US
- Move up the technology curve: first-in-India 20-inch rim size OE tyres for domestic PVs and acoustic foam tyres for EVs for in-cabin noise reduction
